basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE 2020 BANGSAMORO APPROPRIATIONS TO DECEMBER 31, 2021, EXCEPT PERSONNEL SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 47 OF THE GENERAL PROVISIONS OF BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 03, THE BANGSAMORO APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF FISCAL YEAR 2020
basic_information.approved_by: Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim (signed; the date line on the signed copy is blank)
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Gives the Bangsamoro Government one more year to spend its unused 2020 budget for operating costs and projects — but not for salaries, which still had to be used by the end of 2020.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The 2020 budget was due to lapse on 31 December 2020. Passed on 23 December, 8 days before that deadline, the act keeps money already appropriated for projects and operations alive rather than letting it expire unspent in the region's first full budget year.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Money appropriated in 2020 for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses and for Capital Outlay stayed available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2021, under the same conditions it was granted. Personnel Services money was not extended.
who_will_be_affected: Anyone waiting on a project funded by the 2020 budget — it did not have to be cancelled and re-appropriated
Bangsamoro ministries and agencies with unspent 2020 operating and capital funds
The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which issues the guidelines
Taxpayers, since the money stayed in the same purposes rather than reverting
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication, in late 2020. Its operative window has now closed — the extension it granted ended 31 December 2021.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: SPENT AND CLOSED. This gave the region until the end of 2021 to spend leftover 2020 money on operations and projects. Salaries were excluded. The window has since expired.
in_practice: Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses: extended to 31 December 2021
Capital Outlay (buildings, equipment, infrastructure): extended to 31 December 2021
Personnel Services (salaries): NOT extended — valid only to 31 December 2020
The extension kept the original purpose and conditions of each appropriation
Took effect immediately on publication, not after the usual 15 days

for_specific_groups.Communities awaiting a project: A road, building or piece of equipment funded in 2020 could still be paid for through 2021 rather than the money lapsing.
for_specific_groups.Government employees: Nothing changed. Salary appropriations still had to be obligated and disbursed by the end of 2020.
for_specific_groups.Agencies: Unspent operating and capital funds stayed usable for the same specified purposes, under the same general and special provisions.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Historic. The extended period ran out on 31 December 2021.
what_you_can_do: Read this as budget history — it explains why some 2020-funded projects were still being paid for during 2021
watch_out_for: The signed copy carries the Chief Minister's signature but the approval date line is left blank — the registry records the date as unstated rather than inferring one.
The act extends the deadline without adding money or changing what the money was for.
Salaries were deliberately excluded, so an agency could not convert unspent payroll into other spending.

key_terms_explained.MOOE: Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses — the running costs of an office: supplies, utilities, travel, services.
key_terms_explained.Capital Outlay: Money for things that last — buildings, vehicles, equipment, infrastructure.
key_terms_explained.Personnel Services: Salaries, allowances and benefits of government staff.
key_terms_explained.MFBM: The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which issues the guidelines for implementing the extension.
key_terms_explained.Cash Budgeting System: A rule that appropriations must actually be paid out within a set period rather than left open indefinitely.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 23 December 2020. Signed by the Chief Minister; the date of approval is blank on the signed copy.

benefits.headline: Kept a year of project and operating money alive instead of letting it lapse.

direct_benefits.benefit: Projects and operating spending funded in 2020 could continue into 2021
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Communities and agencies with pending 2020-funded work
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic — it changed the deadline, not the process

indirect_benefits: Avoided the cancellation and re-appropriation of work already budgeted in the region's early years

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending deadlines.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), which issues the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A health centre was funded in the 2020 budget but not finished by December. Because of this act the capital outlay stayed available and the work could be paid for during 2021 rather than needing a fresh appropriation.
An agency had unspent salary money at the end of 2020. That was not extended — Personnel Services stopped at 31 December 2020.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 47 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 3, the Bangsamoro Appropriations Act of Fiscal Year 2020, on the Cash Budgeting System. As amended, appropriations for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses and for Capital Outlay remain available for release and disbursement for the purpose specified, under the same general and special provisions, until 31 December 2021. Appropriations for Personnel Services remain valid for obligation and disbursement only until 31 December 2020. The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management is authorised to issue the necessary implementing guidelines.
Section 2 — Repeals or modifies inconsistent laws, decrees, executive issuances, rules and regulations.
Section 3 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation, rather than after the usual 15 days.

impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the life of money already appropriated by Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 3 for fiscal year 2020.
impact.figures_note: The act states no amount — it changes a deadline, not a sum.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The extension it granted expired on 31 December 2021, so the act is spent — it remains on the books but has no continuing operation.

citizen_questions.a: It moved a deadline. Money appropriated in the 2020 Bangsamoro budget for operating expenses and for capital projects could still be released and spent until 31 December 2021 instead of lapsing at the end of 2020.

citizen_questions.q: Did it add money to the budget?
citizen_questions.a: No. It extended the availability of appropriations already made; it granted nothing new and changed no purpose.
The act expressly kept Personnel Services valid only to 31 December 2020. Only Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses and Capital Outlay were extended.
It remains on the books but is spent — the period it extended ended on 31 December 2021.

citizen_questions.q: When did the Chief Minister approve it?
citizen_questions.a: The signed copy carries his signature but the date line is blank. Parliament passed it on 23 December 2020.

views.simple: Extended the life of the 2020 Bangsamoro budget for operating costs and capital projects to 31 December 2021, leaving salary appropriations to expire at the end of 2020.
